title: How to Paint Everything: Marvel Crisis Protocol - Iron Lad
content:
Hey everybody, I'm back with another How to Paint Everything: Marvel Crisis Protocol and this time we are looking for the time-displaced younger version of Kang the Conqueror, Iron Lad! This model can be found in the Iron Lad, Iron Monger, Kang the Conqueror & Rescue Character Pack.

Like many of the "Iron-Suit" characters, Iron Lad's model features a cool blast off effect and this time it features a ring of clouds surrounding the rocket boot blasts. This give a very neat effect that he's punching through the air while flying.

For Iron Lad's paint job, we are going to look at painting non-metallic metal red and silver as well as fire and cloud effects. As always, you can find the colors that were used on this paint job in a handy-dandy paint chart below.

Let's get to it and paint up Iron Lad!

Credit - Brushwizard

Red Armor

Basecoat - Citadel Rhinox Hide

Layer - Citadel Rhinox Hide: Army Painter Dragon Red

Layer - Army Painter Dragon Red

Highlight - Army Painter Angelic Red

Highlight - Army Painter Flickering Flame

Highlight - AK Interactive White

Non-metallic red is one of my favorite things to paint, and the key to it is a nice, solid basecoat of Rhinox Hide. It's such a great color and over the years, it's become a staple for many other color recipes as well. The next step is to mix Rhinox Hide with Dragon Red and paint this onto any areas that will be catching light, while leaving the Rhinox Hide showing. This will enforce contrast later. Next, we paint Dragon Red on top of the previous layer, also leaving the Red and Brown mix showing.

Highlights are started with Angelic Red on top of the previous layer and on all of the sharp edges. This is followed by another edge highlight with Flickering Flame, and finally, another, more controlled highlight of White.

Silver Armor

Basecoat - AK Interactive French Blue

Shadows - AK Interactive Dark Sea Blue

Layer - AK Interactive French Blue

Highlight - AK Interactive Snow Blue

Highlight - AK Interactive White

Dark Lining - AK Interactive Black

Iron Lad's silver armor sections started with a basecoat of French Blue; the shadows and recesses were then painted Dark Sea Blue. This was followed by a clean-up layer of French Blue. Highlights started with a layer of Snow Blue over the French Blue areas and on any edges, followed by another highlight of White. To enforce the contrast, we line the armor panels and recesses with Black.

Repulsor and Eye Glow

Basecoat - AK Interactive White

Layer - Lethal Shadows Fluorescent Light Orange

All of the glowing sections of the armor were given a basecoat of White and a layer of Fluorescent Light Orange.

Blast Effect

Basecoat - Army Painter Warp Yellow

Layer - Army Painter Flickering Flame

Layer - Army Painter Angelic Red

Highlight - Army Painter Aegis Aqua

Highlight - AK Interactive White

The main lower section of the blast-off effect was painted Warp Yellow. Once it was dry, I added a layer of Flickering Flame to it and added a bit of Warp Yellow onto the surface as well, to wet-blend the two colors together. This was followed by a layer of Angelic Red, which was wet-blended into Flickering Flame.

The upper section also started with a layer of Warp Yellow, which was blended into Aegis Aqua near the top of the column of fire. The blast effect under his boot started with Aegis Aqua and was highlighted with White to finish it off.

Cloud Effects

Basecoat - Army Painter Ash Grey

Layer - Army Painter Brigade Grey

Layer - AK Interactive White

The ring of clouds around his blast effect started with a layer of Ash Grey. I then used Brigade Grey and painted globs of grey around the surface of the cloud rings to simulate the shape of the cloud. This was also done with White, overlapping the previous layers.

Concrete Basing

Basecoat - Citadel Stormvermin Fur

Stipple - Army Painter Ash Grey

Stipple - Army Painter Brigade Grey

Wash - Citadel Nuln Oil

As usual, my main go-to for painting concrete basing is to start with a layer of Stormvermin Fur. The surface is then stippled with Ash Grey and Brigade Grey to add a bit of texture to the surface. It's then finished off with a wash of Nuln Oil to get some shadows into the recesses and tie the colors together.

Credit - Brushwizard

Will young Nate break away from the threads of fate and keep himself from becoming Kang the Conqueror? Or is he destined to always return to the mantle of Kang? As always, thanks again for sending this box my way, Atomic Mass Games. Have you picked up the Iron Lad, Iron Monger, Kang the Conqueror & Rescue box? If so, hit me up on Bluesky or Instagram! If you're a Patron of Tabletop Battles, join us in the Marvel: Crisis Protocol channel of our Discord. It's always nice to chat about the game and our hobby projects!

Have any questions or feedback? Drop us a note in the comments below or email us at contact@tabletopbattles.com. Want articles like this linked in your inbox every Monday morning? Sign up for our newsletter. And don't forget that you can support us on Patreon for backer rewards like early video content, Administratum access, an ad-free experience on our website, and subscriber-only content covering competitive Warhammer 40K!

title: [40k] Tabletop Battles Hot Take: Rules Updates for the 2026 World Championships of Warhammer
content:
Games Workshop published a new site today for their Warhammer Events, and with it, the long-awaited rules updates for Warhammer 40,000 ahead of the 2026 World Championships. This rules update, intended for use at the 2026 World Championships, act as a sort of “stopgap” between the September Balance update and the next, outlining a number of rulings and common rules problems ahead of the event, giving players some much-needed guidance on a few things.

In this article, we’ll be covering the changes, what they mean, and just as importantly - what they missed.

Core Rules Updates

Most of the rulings and updates here concern characters, specifically characters attached to units, though there are a few things here about terrain and movement.

Attached Characters

  • Revived characters which come back as a new unit lose their ‘while leading abilities’ benefits
  • If an attached character’s BODYGUARD unit had an enhancement and is destroyed, the character loses the benefit of the enhancement
  • If you split a unit with an attached character into multiple units, only the part of the unit which retains the attached character benefits from the leader’s benefits
  • If you gave an upgrade enhancement to a CHARACTER leader/support unit and attached it to another unit, when your attached character is destroyed, the attached unit loses the effects of the leader’s upgrade enhancement.

Desperate Escape Tests and Units Which Can Move Through Models 

If you fall back with a unit that can move through all types of model, you don’t have to activate Desperate Escape mode when making your Fall Back move. Makes sense, but this serves as a good catchall for abilities that work like fly but aren’t, such as Necrons phasing through walls.

Fighting on Death: Act Like You Have 1 Wound Left

This clears up questions around bracketing on vehicles and other big units.

INFANTRY/BEASTS/SWARM models don’t move vertically when going over dense terrain features that are less than 2” in height.

Not sure I’d ever seen this come up but sure.

Units selected to shoot but which make no attacks remain hidden.

This is a fun quirk, in that you can select a unit to shoot to get some benefit, then opt to make no attacks, and not lose your hidden status. This also applies if you are selected to shoot, but for some reason don't get to (e.g. your opponent activates a Stratagem that stops a unit being targeted. Good for the shoot-and-scoot crowd. Edit: Not quite - our Discord has points out that rule 04.03.04 specifically says that to qualify as having "shot" a unit needs to make at least one attack. Since most shoot-and-scoots happen after a unit has shot, if you make no attacks you won't get to do them. Some of the other things below such as opportunistically deciding not to shoot as AdMech do still work!

TheChirurgeon: This one caused a powerful stir in our competitive discussion channel, because the question of “can you activate a unit to shoot and make zero attacks?” is a touch controversial. As written we believe this to be the case, given the sequence for ranged attacks has you nominate a unit to shoot, then for each model in the unit you can pick one or more ranged weapons that model has to make attacks, giving you the option of picking zero. This also matters for the Adeptus Mechanicus, where the Baffling Data Screed ability on Tech-Priests lets them roll a D6 when their unit is selected and on a 2+, they can stay hidden after shooting. With this particular ruling you can now select them to shoot, roll, and if they fail the role, opt to shoot no weapons and stay hidden, risking nothing.

This also has big implications for the Phobos Strike Force, where the detachment rule lets you choose to stay hidden or move D6” after shooting - now you can opt to shoot and make no attacks, staying hidden and also moving D6”. 

Stratagems with Multiple Targets

You can’t use a Stratagem which requires a stated number of units if you don’t have that many eligible units, i.e. if you need to target two friendly units and you only have one, you’re out of luck.

Devastating Wounds and Damage Modifiers

They’ve added an FAQ stating that abilities that reduce damage work against [DEVASTATING WOUNDS]. One would hope that this comes with an actual rules addendum in the formal update, as it is currently just a “because we said so” FAQ rather than an actual rules entry. Previously whether these abilities worked on Devastating Wounds depended entirely on the specific wording of the effect.

Strategic Reserves and Ingress Moves

  • If you have an ability which allows a unit to to treat the battle round number as one higher than it is for a unit in Strategic Reserves, you can use it to make an ingress move in your first turn.
  • If a unit goes back into Strategic Reserves with an ability that says it has to make an ingress move in the/your next Movement phase, it can do so on the first turn.

These were both pretty clear and used in tenth but somewhere along the way in the transition to 11th wording changed and we needed new clarification for them.

Surge Moves don’t have to go the full distance, apparently.

A model making a surge move doesn’t have to move the maximum distance permitted by the move. What are we even doing here?

Mission Updates

There are four FAQs covered here, three of them relating to Lions of the Emperor and the Unleash the Lions stratagem. The first two cover the unit splitting and persisting effects - for both the Consecration primary mission as well as the Beacon secondary mission they are no longer eligible units for scoring. The third Lions interaction is that if the unit being targeted is condemned, then it does count as leaving the battlefield. All reasonable answers here, nothing too surprising - but good to see clear answers on these.

The last entry is a bit of a head-scratcher - it states that if you are being set up within 6” of the battlefield edge and there is a terrain feature at 6” from the battlefield edge you can perform actions on this terrain feature (e.g. Plunder) or contest it if the terrain feature is an objective.

TheChirurgeon: I don’t understand this at all. If the visible distance between a terrain feature and the edge of the table is 6”, then isn’t it implied that the terrain feature is more than 6” from the edge of the battlefield? How does deploying within 6” put you on the terrain? This suggests that a terrain feature 6” away from the battlefield edge is now considered to be within 6” of the battlefield edge, which OK makes some kind of sense but has really bad implications for terrain features that are on the line of your deployment zone - they’re now “in’ your deployment zone. Thankfully I don’t think this puts any new terrain features/objectives into deployment zones on the current layouts, but that feels more like a bullet dodged.

Faction Updates

Most of these updates cover outstanding FAQs, with some small tweaks to profiles for Space Marines and Chaos Space Marines.

Adepta Sororitas: You can use Miracle Dice Generated from a Character’s Death when they stand back up with Divine Intervention

This resolves an interesting timing question around when those dice are generated and used for the purposes of standing up with more wounds.

Adeptus Custodes: Shield-Captains can use their Master of of Ka’tahs ability to activate both the Dacatarai and Kaptaris abilities in the same phase

Jag the Power Armor Enthusiast: Custodes Shield Captains can in fact activate their stance re-up in the same phase! While this was assumed, the confirmation is very welcomed and makes shield captains even better than they already were.

Unleash the Lions

There were a number of rulings and changes here to a very complicated Stratagem:

  • Using this Stratagem does not count as destroying the unit.
  • The unit does count as having left the battlefield.
  • Using the Stratagem does not spread persisting effects to the split-off models.
  • Using the Stratagem does reload once per Battle Abilities on the split units.
  • Splitting a unit effectively breaks focused abilities like the Blade Champion's +1 to wound as the unit no longer exists but wasn’t destroyed, and a new unit cannot be targeted.

Jag the Power Armor Enthusiast: Lions of The Emperor… GW, Jesus, you had to say this much? To Summate: No, using Lions doesn't count as destroying them; they do count as leaving the battlefield; no, persisting effects do NOT stay on all the models once you use Unleash the Lions. (Failgrim catches another nerf indirectly from this, for the love of Slaanesh GW why do you hate him so much?!) You also now reload an Allarus Captain's once Per Battle abilities if he's part of the Unit that splits off! This is a very good buff for Allarus Shield Captains. Because here, let me teleport him over to push a button or hold an objective late game! Or reload a stance if you used it last round, for just the SC, Dread Host stonks go UP with this little note! We’re still not done! Here, want to make AdMech players and anyone with a targeted +1 to wound or similar ability in general lose the last bit of hope they didn’t even know they still had? Just wait for them to target the unit, and then use unleash the Lions next turn and break it! This certainly won't be a bad idea and cause feels bad moments, nope, not at all!

Aeldari: Dragon Knights can use multiple Dracolithe tokens against the same unit that ended a move within 8”.

Stunt on those hoes.

Astra Militarum: When using Summary Execution or Brutal Disciplinarian to remove battle-shock, you don’t regain the effects of issued orders.

Those soldiers apparently forgot what you were talking about earlier. They’re cool now, though.

Astra Militarum: A battle-shocked Kasrkin unit can use its Warrior Elite ability to pick an order.

This apparently doesn’t count as issuing an order, and you don’t “become” battle-shocked. So they can have an order applied to them, as a treat. You can’t improve your OC with this - it becomes ‘-’ when Battle-shocked - but you can use it to get Take Aim on your last two meltagunners, which is nice.

Blood Angels: Weapons and Base Tweaks

Mephiston’s Plasma Pistol ganed [HAZARDOUS], the plasma pistol on Death Company Captains gained [CLOSE QUARTERS], and the Twin Heavy Bolter on the Death Company Dreadnought has [RAPID FIRE 2]. They did not fix the thunder hammer on the Blood Angels Captain lacking Dev Wounds. Dante is on a 50mm base now in the Tournament Companion.

Chaos Daemons: Pink Horrors can still split if the attached CHARACTER survives.

You’ll have to kill absolutely everything in one activation if you want to avoid splitting.

Chaos Space Marines: Weapon Tweaks

Chaos Bikers get S5 AP-1 combi-bolters and Nemesis Claw get S5 close combat weapons. Sure, now make Bikers 4W like Outriders.

The Deathwatch Terminators Thing

Deathwatch Terminators saw one major change - their plasma cannon was reduced from Strength 9/10 to 7/8, bringing them in line with the plasma cannon wielded by the Deathwing Terminator Squad. They also added a caveat to Dark Angels army rule entry stating that Deathwatch Terminator Squad units do not gain the DEATHWING keyword despite being Terminator units.

Curie: This was needed; for anyone not aware you could run Deathwatch Terminators using the Deathwatch Support detachment and they’d benefit from the Inner Circle Task Force detachment as well, giving them +1 to wound against units on the vowed objective marker. It gave them access to an additional fight on death stratagem, as well as a stratagem for setting up from Deep Strike outside of 6” instead of 8”. As sad as this makes me as someone who was running the army and abusing this interaction, it’s for the better.

Jag the Power Armor Enthusiast: I really don't know if I agree with the decision to punish Deathwatch players’ units for this. Yes it's a needed nerf, but there were better ways to nerf this, especially as this doesn't solve the other major combo of Ultramarines taking DW Terms and using Guilliman and the Terminator Detachment to supercharge two squads. The easier solution would have been to say that Deathwatch Terms do not benefit from other Chapter abilities, so that way the UM/DW Castle of Death doesn't instantly delete armies. Or, hike the points on Plasma Cannons or limit them to one per 5, which would cut down on this problem immediately.

TheChirurgeon: None of these people are “Deathwatch Players,” only people running “Deathwatch Terminators,” and I’ll bet all the money in my pockets that when they do they’re typically painted as some other chapter. But yeah, generally the Deathwatch Terminator situation sucks and the Deathwatch Support Detachment needs to be violently uprooted from the game.

Jag: You are of course right, this is meta chasers abusing what was likely meant as a fluffy detachment but now anyone who wants to play Deathwatch itself catching a stray because of the Competitive Crowd abusing GW's oddball writing choices with Deathwatch on the whole. There are better ways to fix this in my opinion.

TheChirurgeon: I am once again banging a drum labeled “LEGENDS DETACHMENTS” to cover stuff that looks cool and lets armies mix in ways that can break the game.

Jag: Or, you know, add a specific thing, like a mode for narrative play that is long-form, and has consequences and rewards for fluff centric play. It could even have special rules for each army… oh well, such a thing is probably too complex for a small company like Games Workshop.

Death Guard: Shambling Wall Nerfed/Fixed

A set of changes to Shambling Wall make it work as intended in 11th edition, so now you no longer get to roll saves prior to picking up your Poxwalkers. Also note that Devastating Wounds from critical wounds fall outside of this sequence and so can’t be in the pool of wounds that go to your Poxwalkers when you absorb attacks via the Stratagem.

Drukhari: The Double-cross Stratagem

All of these rulings are about the Double-cross Stratagem from the Kabalite Cartel Detachment. This is another ability where you’re passing wounds off to another unit, and now this has been updated to reflect 11th edition sequencing, having your opponent pick a wound in their pool, end the attack sequence, and do mortal wounds equal to the attack’s D characteristic. They then repeat these steps until there are none left. Devastating Wounds don’t add to this pool and can’t be absorbed, and you get to roll your Feel No Pain rolls.

Imperial Agents: Detachment Tweaks

You can theoretically pick Detachments from outside the book now.

Imperial Knights: Sir Hekhtur and Oaths

Canis Rex no longer counts as having left the battlefield until Hekhtur is destroyed, so it won’t trigger key effects like being Condemned. When you make your Lay Low the Tyrant oath as an additional oath for Heroes of Legend, that’s also when you pick the character in your opponent’s army.

Iron Hands: Their Detachments can’t have other Chapters.

A tweak they made across the board here on some Chapter Detachments which were clearly missing some intended wording and allowing for a lot of potential misuse.

Necrons: Triggering Reanimations and Reactive Subroutines

Now when your Warriors get a re-roll on their protocols from being near a Canoptek Reanimator, they also get to re-roll the D3 additional wounds from the Nanoscarab reanimation aura. And if you use the Reactive Subroutines Stratagem on Wraiths, it will trigger the unit’s Wraith Form ability.

Orks: Grot Shields Changes

Both of the Ork items here relate to the Grot Shields Stratagem in the Runt Swarm Detachment. The wording on this has been adjusted and cleaned up so after the hit rolls step, your opponent picks one hit, ends the sequence for it, and does a mortal wound to your GRETCHIN unit. They repeat this steps until they’re out of hits or the Gretchin unit is destroyed. This gives the opponent substantially more power and control over the sequencing of attacks and how they’re allocated, and could make a big difference if they have a lot of different weapon types to throw in. There’s also clarification on how this works with [LETHAL HITS] and [SUSTAINED HITS] - they work as you’d expect.

Raven Guard: Shadowmark can’t have other Chapters.

Thus ends our long national nightmare of Guilliman Shadowmark.

Space Marines: Boltstorm Gauntlets lose [Close-Quarters]; selecting doctrines for a unit doesn’t count for the army doctrines.

Two quick clarifications here and Boltstorm Aggressors take another hit.

Space Wolves: Their Detachments can’t have other Chapters.

Similar to tweaks elsewhere. No, they didn’t fix the stupid Wulfen enhancement. No, we don’t know why they didn’t, either.

Ultramarines: Blade of Ultramar can’t have other Chapters.

Just a common sense move.

World Eaters: Defiler and Rhino Tweaks

The Defiler gets rules specifying the model it shoots with the Unleash Wrath ability had to be set up this phase, while the Rhino’s disembark ability specifies it’s a Rapid Disembark. This means that if it arrived from reserves this turn, the disembarking units cannot be within 8” of any enemy units.

Final Thoughts

This is… well, some of these are fine. The Shamblerot fix needed to happen, as did the Deathwatch and chapter-specific updates. But this document causes a few new problems - the notion that terrain listed as 6” away from a table edge is within 6” of that table edge is… certainly something, and has bigger implications we’ll feel later, I’m sure. The rules on leaving the table are also strange, and not having to move maximum distance with surge moves which say “as close as possible” feels wrong and strange.

title: [Warmachine] Tabletop Battles Reviews: Covenant of the Flame Wave One Releases
content:
The hour of the faithful is finally upon us, Warmachine players. After years of waiting for the Protectorate of Menoth to return in Mark IV, the warriors of Menoth have finally arrived with the new Covenant of the Flame faction. This faction is focused on the forces of the ambitious and zealous Feora, who has returned from her exile to lead the once beaten and broken Protectorate back to its former glory. Feora and her other Warcaster leaders not only command the iconic warjacks of the Protectorate, like the Crusader and the Revenger, but a rebuilt and reinvigorated temple Flameguard.

Visually, the Covenant of the Flame are extremely similar to their old incarnations from the original version of Warmachine, with some updates to modernize each sculpt. In today’s article, Dan “Swiftblade” Richardson will take us through the first new wave of Menoth releases: the Defenders of the Flame army box, as well as the Crusader Heavy Warjack kit and the Revenger Light Warjack.

We would like to thank the Warmachine team for sending us a copy of these models for review.

Credit: Steamforged Games

The Defenders of the Flame Army Box

The Defenders of the Flame Army Box is the primary release of this first wave of new Menoth, and serves as the best jumping off point for both new and old players to pick up the army. It contains 30 points worth of forces, which is enough for a small skirmish game or a learning game, and includes the Warcaster Feora, Marshall of the Flameguard, two character solos in Valeria, The Whisper of Death ad Pyrrhus, Flameguard Commander, a unit of Flameguard Defenders, and one Crusader Heavy Warjack with fixed Weapon options. Since the Crusader also had a separate release, we will cover it in more detail in a later section.

As a longtime Protectorate of Menoth fan, I was very excited to get my hands on these sculpts to see for myself just how much they’ve changed since back in Mark III, especially aside from Valeria, all of these models were returning character or units. I’m happy to say that the Warmachine team did not disappoint in the slightest with these sculpts, and that these new kits are some of the best they’ve ever made.

Feora is the standout in the whole set, with her new model a clear throwback to her original appearance all the way in the very first edition of Warmachine. She arrives in just one piece, so assembling her was simple as putting her on a base and calling it a day. I was also pleasantly surprised that Feora, like all of the other kits in this first wave, required far less cleanup of print supports and leftover bumps, and the resin felt really sturdy compared to older Warmachine releases. Plus, the details on Feora are nice and crisp, nothing was muddy looking following the print. Its a sign of just how far Warmachine has come from its troubled Mark IV release, and the team should be proud.

The two character solos are similarly high quality, though I do have small notes on both. For Valeria, because of her dynamic pose (which rocks), she’s more delicate than the other models in the box, and the brick that she’s leaping off of had broken off from the rest of the wall during shipment. Fortunately, she has multiple points of contact with her base, and fixing this very minor issue is as easy as a little superglue, but I would advice anyone to be careful handling her compared with the other models. Pyrrhus is the only character model in this whole box with multiple parts, as his spear and shield needs be be glued on separately, and honestly the only model that I think is a step down from his original look. The sculpt itself is a much higher quality, don’t get me wrong, but Pyrrhus’s original model was posed far more dynamically, like he was leaping into the fight, while his updated version as the Commander of the Flameguard is instead posed like he is about to throw his flaming spear, coupled with several extra spears on his back once he throws the first. This is bizarre, since he has no ranged options to speak of, and makes me think that an older version of his rules may have featured a thrown weapon option that was later scrapped. Still, this is a pretty minor grievance, and the filigree on some of the armor as well as Pyrrhus’s face are very detailed.

The Flameguard Defenders are really the only models in the box I had any issues with. Starting off on a positive note here, the new Flameguard Defenders kit looks great, and I love the updated look from the robes of the OG Flameguard to these new armored versions. They keep the same iconic silhouette and helmet, but the new armor sets them apart and looks cool as hell. As for the issues, the first one I had is something that I think everyone assembling these models will run into, which is the fact that there’s no instructions or indications as for what spear and shield goes with each body. There’s not a whole ton of parts here, so this was solved with some very simple and pain free trial and error.

The second issue isn’t going to affect everyone, but it's one I ran into with this box alongside several other boxes I’ve ordered lately, and that’s the dreaded mispack. When I opened up my Defenders, I found that I’d only received one shield instead of five. Like I said, I’ve run into a few mispacks and misprints now, so I’m familiar with how to contact the Warmachine customer service team and in their defense, the customer service team has been nothing but polite and helpful. On top of this, when I received the second Defenders of the Flame box I’d ordered for myself a few days later, there were no mispacks to speak of, so the incorrect number of shields is just an issue with my army box and not every single release. Frankly, on its own it's a minor gripe, and I wouldn’t bring it up here if this was just an isolated incident. But I had multiple issues with both mispacks and misprints in recent purchases of new Fane kits as well as this Flameguard kit, and it's frequent enough that it can’t be ignored when reviewing these kits. The high frequency of mispacks and misprints, even on boxes that have been marked with a quality stamp, are a major problem that Steamforged needs to address quickly as Warmachine continues to grow, or new players are going to bounce off the game fast.

The Crusader Heavy and Revenger Light Warjacks

The Crusader and Revenger kits are just amazing; I love these sculpts so much as someone who remembers these kits from over a decade ago. Both of them are a perfect example of what an update to an old kit should be, which is taking something the past and modernizing it without making it look so different that it’s unrecognizable. Between the two, the Revenger is the most similar to its original version, as it’s nearly a one to one reincarnation fo the old kit with the addition of some extra cloth and decorative shoulder plates. The Crusader kit on the other hand looks like the Crusader had a minor makeover for his new lease on life, with bulkier shoulder plates and extra decorative plates. There is a weird bit with the Crusader kit that the model on the box is a little different from the actual model inside; there are some shoulder plates that aren't present in the release version of the kit and the feet are slightly different. This doesn’t detract from the quality of the kit, but it is important to note so you don’t go scrambling around to try and find the those bits.

Like all of the cohort models released in Mark IV, the Crusader and Revenger are built with magnetization in mind, and both of these kits have some minor changes that make magnetization much easier. First, both the Crusader and the Revenger use the same magnet size (5mm by 2mm), which is a nice quality of life update as now you don’t need to to purchase one set of magnets for the light cohort and one for the heavy. The second thing to note is that the arm joints now have little nubs to help the models arms fit snugly when placed, so there are no worries here about the arms spinning and makes the kit feel very sturdy to handle.

Credit: Dan "Swiftblade" Richardson

Time constraints prevented me from painting nearly as many of these models as I’d hoped to with this release, but I did pull some light nights and painting marathons to get at least one Crusader done and man, this kit looks incredible once it's brought to life in color. It's the perfect ideal of what a Warjack should be: Big, bulky, and menacing, and the addition of more decorative armor plates add a sort of ceremonial reverence to the machine that vibes well with the holy crusaders theme of the Covenant of the Flame. Traditionally, the Protectorate has always been the faction in Warmachine that leans the most heavily into fielding multiple Warjacks, which is great news for me since both of these new Warjack kits are a slam dunk.

Final Thoughts

Comparison between the old Vanquisher and new Crusader. Credit: Dan "Swiftblade" Richardson

While the issues I had here with the mispack are very serious and I hope the Warmachine team is able to heavily reduce this in the future, overall the first wave of new Covenant of the Flame models is a complete triumph. title: The biggest chase cards in MTG Star Trek
content:
With MTG Star Trek just one week away, and prerelease events kicking off tomorrow, it's not long before fans will be getting their hands on Magic: The Gathering's latest Universes Beyond set. If you're planning to crack packs and want to know what cards constitute a big hit, this guide will break down the highest value pulls you can find in a Play Booster.

That's right, we're only looking at the regular cards and treatments available in Play packs. We're a publication by the people, for the people, so if you want to know what the top cards you can pull in a Collector Booster are (It's almost definitely a Patrick Stewart signed card) then you'll have to look elsewhere.

One last note, I've left off the exact prices for these cards, since at this early stage they're likely to fluctuate wildly and would be instantly outdated. For the stardate reprint cards, which make up much of this list, I've included the price of the cheapest version currently available.

Dr. Beverly Crusher

It's a new type of doubler effect - the life gain triggers doubler. This three mana card is absolutely perfect for lifegain decks, making stuff like Ajani's Pridemade twice as good. However, Bev hangs out at the bottom of this list because she's a lot narrower than she actually appears and likely to drop in price.

The effect doesn't double life gained, nor abilities that check whether life was gained in a turn. It's specifically abilities that trigger when life is gained that this creature cares about.

Captain Jean-Luc Picard

One of the best mono-white commanders I've seen in a while, Captain Picard creates crew members, and when you have enough of them he can tutor spacecraft into play already stationed. There's some neat synergy with the Edge of Eternity card, The Seriema - theoretically if Picard was hit with removal you could tap him and six officers to pull it into play and make him indestructible - neat.

There's another likely reason this card is looking popular currently - Patrick Stewart's sad death last week. Whether you see it as a touching tribute or just a bit ghoulish, the fact remains that a card's connection to a recently deceased celebrity gives it a significant popularity boost - as we last saw with Optimus Prime.

LCARS Shocklands

These powerful lands have come down in value a long way since I first got into Magic, with reprint after reprint making them more accessible. Still, they are always in extremely high demand, and these full art versions are bound to be even more so. Especially since they're textless, so you'll have to be eagle-eyed to stop folks bringing them in untapped and not paying their two life!

Shizo, Death's Storehouse

Cheapest version: $37

If your deck is black and wants to attack it can use Shizo, Death's Storehouse. Since that's an enormous number of decks, this utility land is understandably pricey. This version, reskinned as the Terran Throne Room, shows off a location from Star Trek's own evil Echoverse.

Bruvac, the Gradiloquent

Cheapest version: $45

Spock appears here as probably the best mill creature of all time. Bruvac has only ever been released in limited numbers - in Jumpstart, Ravnica Remastered, and Secret Lair - which has kept the price surprisingly high.

Minamo, School at Water's Edge

Cheapest version: $60

One of the best utility lands Magic has, School at Water's Edge is king of combos, a cEDH staple and also just really, really useful with any Commander that has a tap ability.

Sheoldred, The Apocalypse

Cheapest version: $88

While Benedict Cucumberpatch, The Apocalypse has generated a ton of memes, you're kidding yourself if you think the mirth surrounding this card means it's going to be any less expensive. Hilariously, this is the most valuable MTG Star Trek card you can pull from a regular booster.

If you're going to a prelease tomorrow, come tell us about it over on the Wargamer Discord.

title: The rarest and most expensive Lorcana cards of 2026
content:
What are the rarest, most expensive Lorcana cards? When the characters and films are so beloved by so many, it only makes sense mega-fans are prepared to shell out for a rare Disney card with unique art of their favorite character. This guide covers all the most expensive Disney Lorcana card sales from the most recent sets.

Disney Lorcana may be the newest of the big trading card games, but it has a dedicated fanbase of collectors who will pay a princess' ransom to get their hands on the most coveted cards. Older TCGs may have higher price ceilings - nothing on this list can match the most expensive rare Pokémon cards or expensive Yugioh Cards - but there are some very valuable cards nonetheless! The most expensive Lorcana cards are:

Elsa, Spirit of Winter (Enchanted) - $720

The original Elsa from 2023's The First Chapter set is already a collectible card, but this full art Enchanted variant is in another league. She's a double threat - not just one of the most popular Disney characters of all time, but the first card printed of that character when the game launched. If you've got one, don't let it go…

Hades, Looking for a Deal (Iconic) - $1,067

This is currently the rarest Disney villain card around! Though released alongside the previous Pocahontas in winterwear, and just as rare, this card took a lot longer to rise to the heights. Maybe it's because Hades isn't a princess? Still, this sneaky backstabber spent all of August closing the distance, and finally overtook her just before the month ended, capping out at a high of $1,200 in September.

Cinderella, Unintentional Icon (Iconic) - $1,152

Yes, she's serving. Released in October as part of Hyperia City, Cinderella's highest sale was a cool $1,500. We can understand why she's running behind set-companion Mickey Mouse - Best in Town, thanks to that more dynamic art, but this is no mean performance.

Moana, Curious Explorer (Iconic) - $1,249

Moana was a surprise appearance in Winterspell, a set with a Winter theme, and it seems this explorer's curiosity is so great she didn't have time to dress for the colder weather. Nevertheless, this paper-cut inspired artwork is absolutely adorable, and helps to make this Iconic card so legendary.

Winnie the Pooh, Hunny Wizard (Enchanted) - $1,430

The colors here are making us so hungry. Pooh Bear doesn't have any fancy abilities to show off, but he does have a soothing smile, a fancy cloak, and golden, sugary goodness surrounding him. Those base stats aren't too shabby, either. By the end of August, Winnie the Pooh was getting close to Ariel, after a long time jockeying for position with Moana.

Ariel, Ethereal Voice (Iconic) - $1,482

This ghostly 'Whisper' of Ariel from the Whispers in the Well set not only has a commanding performance, she also commands a high price on the secondary market, which has only crept up since she released - the last sale, in September, hit $1,550

Lilo and Stitch, Fun-Loving Friends (Iconic) - $1,526

There's so much energy and mischief in this Lilo and Stitch card. It looks like the box art for a straight-to-DVD sequel to the classic movie, and we mean that with love: there's no way any actual animation could live up to the sheer action this promises!

Merida - Formidable Archer (Iconic) - $1,828

We all know that Lorcana is a pacifist game, and nobody involved in a challenge is ever hurt - but we have to wonder what Merida does with her arrows to keep her opponents from getting hurt! This is one of the most dynamic princes poses in all of Lorcana. While TCG player's market price is high, recent sales have all been far lower, around $900.

Belle and Beast, Certain as the Sun (Iconic) - $1816

A card as romantic as this was destined to be sought after - Belle and Beast waltzing is a timeless scene from the film that kicked off the Disney Renaissance.  They're also remarkably faithful to their original on-screen appearance as well. After dipping in September, the market valuation is back close to its original $2,000 mark.

Mickey Mouse - Best in Town (Iconic) - $1,861

Of course a new Mickey Mouse would sell like hot cakes - or hot dogs, as this jaunty take on the many-skilled rodent shows. Hyperia City only became available in October so this card is still being opened, but early sales have all clustered around that $2,000 mark. Time will tell if this is his high water mark, or merely the beginning.

Minnie Mouse, Sweetheart Princess (Iconic) - $3,083

When the first Iconic cards were created for Lorcana they were immediately way pricier than anything else on the market, and nearly made it into the all-time top 10, up against extremely rare early promos. Minnie, blowing a kiss in her medieval princess garb, was beginning to slip from her initial high position on the list - but made a recovery in late August as a sheer lack of supply drove up the market price. By October, she was back with a vengeance, with a high sale of $4,200 that's higher than Mickey has ever sold for!

Buzz Lightyear, Jungle Ranger (Iconic) - $3,613

When Wilds Unknown released Buzz Lightyear quickly became the second most valuable card you can open in a booster pack, topping out at $5,700 for a copy. Sales tailed off in June but it's had a few $3,600 sales since then, and it seems that's where it's stabilized.

Mickey Mouse, Brave Little Prince (Iconic) - $3,875

A copy of Mickey hasn't sold since July, so TCG Player's market valuation of $3,875 is very much an extrapolation from the last time the card moved and what would happen if one were to go on sale again. A sudden flurry of movement could result in Mickey being tipped from the top spot, or confirmed in his crown.

If you're a Lorcana collector but not yet a player, you should fix that immediately! It's easy to learn, and we can talk you through which Lorcana starter decks are worth playing.

title: Mayday, Miss Marcy! Gifted With Yet More Gift Questions
content:
Happy November, and if you happen to live in the United States, Happy Bluenami! November really has just started but wow did it start with quite an energetic start to things. We're back with another installment of advice that you can use, hopefully, as Mayday, Miss Marcy! enters into the final stretch of 2026. Funny to be saying that, as it feels like things just got started! Ah, the prism of time. Anyway! If you're new to this column, we take reader submitted questions and produce the best possible answers we can, and this week, we have... yet more questions about gifts! I guess I have to admit that I'm not surprised as the time for gift giving approaches, and maybe I have to say that I'm proud of people for trying to do it in advance! Always better to be safe than sorry.

If you'd like your questions answered here, please read the information below:

Have a question you want answered on just about anything you’d need advice on in this grand hobby space of ours? Board games, 40k, AOS, TTRPGs, MTG, anything and everything that we cover, we can help with!

For some examples, take a look at previous editions of our column at this link with a handy tag to see all previous questions and answers!

If you want to submit questions, we have a few ways you can do it. Patrons can use the Discord bot command to ask questions, which will be received anonymously!

If you’re not a Patron, or just don’t want extra steps, you can comment on this article, or e-mail me directly at marcy@tabletopbattles.com!

And now without further ado, let us move on to the questions themselves!

Gifted Student

Dear Marcy,

I'm writing today because I have a sort of odd situation at least by my own estimation. I am approaching graduation for my first degree this coming Spring, and this fall is very likely my last semester to work with a particular professor as far as I can tell. They've been one of my biggest supporters and also a semi-advisor, so I suspect I'll still try to talk to them but we won't really have any time to work together. I was wanting to get them a gift before I do, but I'm wondering if a painted miniature is... a lame gift for someone who doesn't play or engage with a hobby? But I have talked about it before and they've known me for a few years now, so I thought it felt more personal than a gift card or something.

Thanks,

Student of the Arts

Dear Student,

I don't think there's anything wrong at all with your idea! If anything, I personally find it pretty touching and personal. You are right, it is different than a gift card, and while most educators would be happy with some extra cash in their pockets (even in gift card form), it sounds to me like you want this professor to remember you. A painted miniature that you give them to remind them of the impact they had on you would probably make their day, since it also becomes something they could display in their office (either at home or at the school), it would serve as a pretty nice reminder that they had an impact and don't just sit around grading assignments all day for faceless people who don't think about them at all. Obviously, there's some limits or considerations here; you probably want to paint something that they might actually like, or at least, something that might appeal to them, rather than just handing them a painted Space Marine and going 'I made this for you'. So think out of the box a bit!

A Spouse's Dream

Dear Miss Marcy,

My partner does not enjoy Warhammer, and I've never really managed to get them to try the game or anything. They sometimes express interest in what I'm painting or the more detailed models that seem intricate, but even then they don't seem like they actually want to interact with it. However, I have been long wondering if perhaps I could get them into the game somehow. I feel like this is a type of question or pipe dream for a lot of people, and while I am being vague, I'm going to just say that we aren't the traditional couple someone might envision here, but at least in this aspect it is a one sided sort of hobby interest. I don't even really know if I want them to play/paint/participate, but it does feel like it would be nice.

Puzzled Partner

Dear Puzzled,

I love when questions are extremely vague and almost making it into a puzzle for me to decipher, but since this is all I have, I will hold off making assumptions; to be honest they don't matter that much anyway, but I can tell by the one comment you made that it is unlikely this is a cis-het man/wife sort of partnership, so if anything that is helpful if anything to avoid stereotyping. That being said, I think you are correct; over the years of doing this column we've had a few questions about spouse participation and disinterest in the hobby, and I think my advice remains mostly the same: you can't make someone like your hobby the way you like your hobby. They might like you, they might appreciate that you have a hobby, but they do not like the hobby itself, and you are unlikely to make them like it. When your spouse makes comments about the painting you're doing, there's a level to it that is perhaps simply signaling visibility: they recognize the time and effort you're making and want to be supportive or interested.

Don't worry about making them get into it; if they wanted to, they'd let you know more clearly. If you tend to do your hobbying in a room all by yourself or as a "you time" thing, they may also simply be respecting that because that's the vibe you've given off. If that isn't the intent, or you have the ability to, consider doing some of your hobbying (like building or painting) with your spouse nearby; perhaps talk to them and chat while you both do something different. And if that isn't what they want, then don't stress; you didn't say they are dismissive or hate what you do, just that they don't seem to want to do it themselves!

Tone Pro Policed

Dear Miss Marcy,

Am I weird for not finding the new tone pro paints interesting? I feel like people were buzzing about them a bit but I have not seen much, and I don't really seem to have any reason to use them myself. The armies I play don't really seem to use the colors people keep saying are must uses, and I really like the paints I already have. But when people talk about them and I say I'm not interested, it seems like I'm the weird one; is it just the idea of FOMO talking, or is not being interested in a new release like this just normal?

Painted

Dear Painted,

We had a similar question a few weeks ago, to which I offered the same comment: HOW are you saying you are not interested? Are you saying "I don't think they're for me" (fine) or are you saying "They look lame as shit lmfao" (not fine). Because one of these, as noted by the parenthetical comments, is a way of explaining that you do not feel interested in something for yourself, but that others may like it, while the other is more akin to the dismissive and generally abrasive tone people use online.

But assuming it isn't the latter, my answer is... sure, why wouldn't it be normal? You aren't required to be excited about things the way everyone else is, and when it comes to something like painting, it really just depends on what you already do and how you like to do it. If you've got a particular style and workflow set up, then you really aren't strange for not finding a new item of interest to you. You say that you don't think the paints would help you much, so that also feels normal; and considering the price of paint, there's really nothing weird about not wanting to speculate about spending money on a thing you don't want or may not use solely to say that you did use and didn't like it. Just don't be an annoying hater about things and you won't really have much of a problem; the biggest issue is not being aware of the fact that the things you say to other people carry more than just what it says on the package, so to speak; if you're being overly dismissive and rude, people are going to be weirded out by it since what you are doing is telling them that their opinions on something completely personal (a type of paint) is somehow not worth giving a normal response to.

Have any questions or feedback? Drop us a note in the comments below or email us at contact@tabletopbattles.com. Want articles like this linked in your inbox every Monday morning? Sign up for our newsletter. And don't forget that you can support us on Patreon for backer rewards like early video content, Administratum access, an ad-free experience on our website, and subscriber-only content covering competitive Warhammer 40K!

title: This unofficial Warhammer 40k web client is the kind of training tool I wish GW would make
content:
Despite increasing digital support for miniature wargames, it's rare to find official digital clients that allow you to play virtual versions of games over the internet. Fans tend to fill the gap: War Table supports Warmachine, Eldfall Chronicles, Malifaux, and Guildball, and for just about everything else there are Tabletop Simulator mods. But a new contender has appeared: 'The Old Wargamer', still in development, is a platform that lets you play both Warhammer: The Old World and Warhammer 40,000 in your browser.

The site's mission statement says it's "an unofficial practice tool to learn the games by playing them, where every charge, wound, save and break test is rolled on screen and explained rather than hidden". I've only had a very basic fiddle with each client, but that intent shines through: the site prioritizes surfacing the rules and making explicit what you can do, must do, and can't do at every phase of the game, and it controls the flow of events through phases in a way I've found easy to parse.

Battles are represented in simple 2D that will give older gamers nostalgic flashbacks to 1990s White Dwarf battle reports. Beside them sits a whole panel dedicated to information about the current phase, the unit you may have selected, and the choices you can make.

Creators Ab1t & Dorreah say that they've summarized the rules for the Old World in their own words, with reference to the fan maintained Online Rules Index, while the points and unit options are imported from Old World Builder. Rules for Warhammer 40k factions are taken from Wahapedia's data export.

While the engine doesn't offer a complete simulation of every rule in either game, the framework covers the critical core systems, and the developers have been posting regular updates and bug fixes. The creators specify that they're paying for AI for the website but not how they're using it; presumably as a coding assistant, but perhaps to provide AI opponents for the single-player mode.

You can find details of how to register with the website on Reddit. Whether the web hosting can keep up with increased demand is a real question for this kind of fan project!

Digital wargame clients can be a helpful dojo to practise with an army before you commit to buying it, and allow physically distant players to play friendly matches or participate in virtual tournaments - they really took off during COVID lockdowns. The Old Wargamer's goal of adding much more scaffolding and rules explanation is a smart one. Done right, this could be an excellent training aid, whether you're learning the basics, memorizing your army rules, or really honing your play.

It would be great for Games Workshop to make an official client similar to this, but I can see why it's not a high priority. In this stripped back form it's a tool for people who are already fairly au fait with strategy games even if they're new to Warhammer, and GW doesn't struggle to recruit that audience. Turning it into something more elaborate, a fully fledged Warhammer 40k videogame with the panache to draw in a wider audience and justify an MSRP on Steam is a much bigger and more risky proposition, not least because the game's core systems will need to be reworked every three years. I hope one or the other version happens, but it seems unlikely.

What do you think? What's your preferred way to play Warhammer online when you can't get a game IRL? What tools did you find most useful in helping you learn to play? Share your thoughts in the Wargamer Discord community!

title: [Kill Team] Looking Back on Approved Ops 2025
content:
The next season of Kill Team, Armageddon, was teased earlier this year at the Big Autumn Preview show, alongside the new Approved Ops deck for 2026. With how the release schedules following that preview tend to go, its likely that we will see these new rules for the game sooner rather than later, putting us at the tail end of the Approved Ops 2025 season. With that in mind, a few of our Kill Team writers sat down and gave their thoughts on the last Season of Kill Team, providing their thoughts on the good, the bad, and the ugly of Approved Ops 2025.

The Good

Credit: Dan "Swiftblade" Richardson

Things we liked about Approved Ops 2025.

James ‘Boss Grubbz’ Grubbs: Approved Ops 2025 improved upon its previous iteration by adding tactical variety to its Crit Ops mission pack. Allowing players multiple avenues to score Victory Points from, incentivized different playstyles and approaching each match up in a unique way. Whether it was Plant Banner forcing a contest over a critical Tac Op point or needing one more kill to advance your Kill Grade and secure the victory in Turning Point 4, there were plenty of opportunities for fun game interactions. Most of the Crit Ops encouraged interaction, though I did find a few lacking in that department.

TheArmorOfContempt: Crit Ops were expanded and diverse enough to make matches feel different in one's strategic approach, while Primary Op introduced a new element for players to track and plan around. While there continues to be issues with Tac Ops this most recent iteration of them was superior to those that came before with less options that were of no use to any team, and instead certain options only being useful to certain teams. While this feels like a backhanded compliment it's important to say that despite all its flaws Approved Ops 2025 was superior to the previous mission pack.

Swiftblade: Games Workshop made a pretty concerted effort for doing rebalancing passes on Approved Ops 2025 to address the balance between Tac Ops post launch, and I think they deserve their flowers for that. While there are folks who whine whenever GW makes sweeping balance updates and changes, ultimately keeping their finger on the pulse of the metagame and addressing Tac Op options that feel either under or overpowered is better for players both on the casual and competitive ends of the spectrum. The dream is that when Approved Ops 2026 releases, it’s perfect on the first try and doesn't need any rebalancing ever, but realistically that's just not going to happen. If it can’t be perfect, then I hope Games Workshop continues to try and keep on top of balance and errata.

As for the mission deck itself, I was very impressed on how much better the Tac Ops were in Approved Ops 2025 versus 2024. AO24 had a real problem where Infiltration had basically no “good” options for Tac Op selection, while Seek and Destroy and Security both had Tac Op options that would vary wildly in usefulness depending on what team you were playing, who you were up against, or even the map. Recon was the only archetype that had reliable options, to the point where having access to Recon Tac Ops was a significant power boost for a team, and being stuck with Infiltration was an albatross around a teams neck. While Recon is still the clear winner out of the four again, each archetype has at least one Tac Op that is very playable no matter what team, and honestly the only real dud Tac Op is Track Intelligence from Infiltration. If the design team improves on the AO25 Tac Ops with AO26, I think we are in for a real treat next season.

The Bad

Credit: Games Workshop

Things that didn’t quite work, and how we hope they can be improved in Approved Ops 2026.

Benjamin “Toll” Scott: Initiative was a hotly contested topic going into Approved Ops 2025. Players can make every decision correctly and still lose the game because they just happen to be on the lower end of four rolls of a die. Rightly, Games Workshop decided to do something about it, but initiative cards didn’t quite have the landing or impact they probably desired. Many times players will simply save their initiative cards for the final turning point, often meaning players will both be at a functional +3. While the ability to use the cards to subtract from your roll adds some decision making in theory, in practice I rarely if ever saw this function used. Ultimately, the cards often brought little if any change to a game and their intended use was rendered moot. Initiative still needs some changes, and hopefully AO26 brings something exciting with it.

Swiftblade: I agree with Ben here on the initiative cards. I remember when these were first announced, there was a widespread panic that these would somehow break the game, and instead ended up being little more than a wet fart. They never really felt like they would make or break a game, they either didn’t really end up mattering for the initiative rolls or a player would have such a huge bonus to their roll that it was basically advertised in neon lights that they would win the initiative the following turning point, and you would just plan accordingly. In a weird way, the initiative cards incentivized losing dice rolls, as losing the roll off for TP 1 and 2, where going first usually wasn’t a big deal, meant you could stock up on initiative bonuses for the late game where it mattered. Wanting to lose a dice roll is counterintuitive and weird. I like rolling big, I don’t want to be excited to roll small. That's the way of the coward.

I’d like to see GW return to something more like the Scouting phase from AO24, the rock-paper-scissors concept for determining first turn initiative was pretty neat in theory. Its biggest problem was the fact that the Equipment scouting choice was almost always the best, which threw off the whole system, but if they can make the possible selections more balanced between one another I think it would be much more engaging than the current initiative cards.

TheArmorOfContempt: Failure to update Gallowdark and Bheta-Decima. This last year of Kill Team can essentially be viewed as the year of Volkus and Tomb World, which is a shame because there is no reason they couldn’t of provided layouts to improve and fix the issues with Gallowdark and Bheta-Decima, which in essence cut the amount of viable maps in half.

James ‘Boss Grubbz’ Grubbs: While Kill Grade is a great idea for improving game interactivity and incentivizing getting into skirmishes, it is not the best implementation of this. Some of the break points in the chart can make for an extremely uphill battle. Short of dominating the Kill Zone and tabling your opponent, which could be quite challenging to accomplish into defensive playstyles, there were plenty of times where you could win Crit Op and Tac Op and still lose the game on Kill Op.

Credit: Warhammer Community

The Ugly

Things that just did not work and we hope don’t come back.

TheArmorOfContempt: Lack of play testing; Tac Ops and Archetypes continue to be based on vibes as opposed to how a team actually plays. While this problem is not new to this Approved Ops Pack, we continue to see that some Tac Ops are literally unplayable depending on your team. For example Martyrs is fantastic in the hands of a horde team, while it is a fast track to auto loss if played by elites. The Archetype system exacerbates this issue by locking Tac Ops into categories.

James ‘Boss Grubbz’ Grubbs: The initiative cards. Initially this felt very convoluted to understand and once that changed it was admittedly easier. That doesn’t mean it was a good solution for initiative. It did improve upon the previous Approved Ops initiative system, but left for some ugly Tac Op interactions with Tac Ops like Data and Download where it felt bad to win initiative all game and still lose because you couldn’t stop them going first Turning Point 4. A flat +2/-2 or giving a reroll to whoever doesn’t have initiative would be simple solutions.

Swiftblade: There are a few crit ops that are real stinkers here. I don’t know if anyone, in the history of ever, enjoyed playing Energy Cells, and Orb is just brutal if you don't have as many activations as your opponent. I get that we are trying to branch out here with designing these Crit Ops, but I’d really prefer that we keep all of these to selections that feel fun and exciting no matter what team you’re running.

I also really hope that for the next release cycle isn’t nearly as long as the gap between Approved Ops 2025 and 2026 has been. As of this writing, we’re still waiting on an announcement for when AO26 will be released, putting us at least 14 months since the main missions and the game were updated. By the time a year rolled around, everyone was ready for a new set of missions, maps, and ops to shake up the game, so being saddled with two (if not more) more months is a real slog. Next time, I hope that Games workshop keeps the release window as timely as possible to avoid this drain on the community at large.

AO2025 Highlights

Some personal highlights or games from this season of Kill Team.

James ‘Boss Grubbz’ Grubbs: Getting the most out of 4 APL Operatives and doing as many actions as possible in one activation. Playing Kommandos and Scout Squad most of this Approved Ops cycle allowed me the opportunity to use 4 APL operatives. This let me squeeze up to as many as 5 actions out of these operatives using an Ammo Cache. The peak of this for me was my Boss Nob getting me a triple kill with an Ammo Cache, Charge, Fight, Fight, Shoot a Harpoon into one of my local players. Doing Gork and Mork justice.

Swiftblade: I mean, the easy highlight for my time with AO2025 is winning Best Overall at the Dallas Open this year. It's an achievement that I’m very proud of, as it was a culmination of all of the hard work I’d put in for both becoming better at playing the game as well as with painting the models. I’d been gunning hard to win Best Overall at Dallas, though I tried everything in my power to play it cool and not get my hopes up during the event. Oh, but when my name was called, the vindication that shot through my body was amazing. Just electric. I felt like I was walking on air the whole way to grab that Golden ticket, and I’m pumped to travel to Barcelona later this year to play at Worlds and give AO2025 one last ride!

title: Pokémon TCG Delta Reign preorders delayed over checkout bug
content:
Pokémon TCG fans who preordered the Delta Reign ETB are frustrated, as this product has been delayed until "mid-November" - suggesting collectors won't get it until at least a week after the set's November 6 release date.

This seems to have been confirmed only in the UK, but US fans say they have not yet been charged for Delta Reign products. The Pokémon Center checkout has been down for a whopping six days, undergoing maintenance.

The delays appear to be connected to a problem with the online store's checkout process. Many UK customers received emails last week asking them to reauthorize payment details by November 4, but consistently found they were unable to do so.

According to one Reddit user's (unverified) communication with support staff, in fact, every customer in the UK was sent one of these emails, apparently in error.

Now the Pokémon Center store is down for maintenance while the problem gets patched. A notice on the Pokémon Center UK website has stated that users should disregard the November 4 deadline for updating their details, saying that if they need to do so, there will be an opportunity later. This heavily implies that not everyone who was told their payment details didn't work will need to take any action.

Naturally, this is frustrating for fans who were hoping to get their cards as close to release as possible, but at least some communication has now started to flow. Pokémon YouTuber PtcgRadio was one of those affected and spoke about trying to fix the issue for days, stressing about missing out as the deadline loomed nearer.

The Pokémon Center's notice also says it expects the Delta Reign ETB boxes to ship by mid-November, though the longer the website stays down for, the more likely further lateness starts to seem.

What is far less clear right now is how widespread the issue is. While communication has been specific to the UK, users from the US say they've not been charged when they expected to be and the store is currently down for everyone.

Have you been affected by this issue? Let us know over on the Wargamer Discord.
